plan.interpretation: I interpreted this as a one-email acquisition introduction for a product manager or product team lead at a software company who may be evaluating how to capture product feedback from customer conversations. The reader's installed tools and current workflow are unknown, so the argument is conditional and the single next step is to get started on Canny's Free plan.
plan.reader:
Selected audience: Product manager or product team lead at a software company.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): People responsible for product decisions at software companies pull customer feedback from multiple channels (sales/CS calls recorded in tools like Gong, support tickets, Slack) into a central place such as a feedback portal or ProductBoard so requests can be reviewed by the product team rather than lost across departments.
plan.reader_segment: Product manager or product team lead at a software company
plan.promise: Canny can turn customer conversations into request-level product feedback and merge duplicate requests, so product teams can work from the requests rather than whole-call links.
plan.orientation: Canny is customer feedback management and product roadmapping software that pulls feedback out of channels like Gong, Intercom and Slack into one place and merges duplicate requests.
plan.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognizing Canny as another feedback tool to seeing one concrete workflow worth trying: Autopilot extracts feature requests from conversations and merges duplicates, with Feedback Discovery available on the Free plan.
plan.sequence_rationale: A single acquisition email should lead with the strongest job-relevant operation, not a catalogue of plans and integrations. The request-level extraction mechanism directly addresses the documented problem with passing entire call links downstream, while the Free-plan availability lowers the commitment of the next step. The brief keeps fine-grained Slack routing, revenue-weighted prioritization, setup effort, and customer time savings outside the promise because the licensed evidence does not establish them for this path. No alternative proposition is included because the available testimonial would support a different customer's outcome more strongly than a general outcome for this reader. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign is a readable copy of the unavailable Canny source page or verification of its missing details.

emails.selection_reason: Extracting individual feature requests from calls, tickets, and reviews addresses the documented downstream problem more directly than leading with integrations, pricing, or a broad feedback-management claim. Free-plan access gives this solution-aware reader a concrete, lower-commitment way to assess that workflow.

email.body:
If customer feedback arrives through calls, tickets, or reviews, Canny Autopilot reads those sources, pulls out individual feature requests, and merges detected duplicates. Your product team can review the requests themselves instead of treating each full conversation as the feedback unit.

Canny is customer feedback management and product roadmapping software. It brings feedback into one place and turns conversations into organized, request-level input for product decisions.

Feedback Discovery is included on Canny’s Free plan with **no Autopilot-credit limit**. Free includes **25 tracked users**, and users whose feedback Autopilot finds count toward that limit.

You can set a monthly spend limit to pause upgrades when it is reached, giving you control as feedback volume grows. Create a Free account to see whether request extraction and duplicate merging fit your team’s intake process.

reads.what_it_sells: Canny offers customer-feedback and roadmapping software that would extract individual feature requests from conversations, tickets, and reviews, merge duplicates, and put the resulting requests in one place for product review.
reads.relevance_feedback: The role fit is explicit: I lead product work at a software company, and the email conditionally addresses feedback arriving through several channels. The broader profile documents this as a real product-management workflow and identifies full recordings as poor downstream feedback units. However, it does not establish that my team currently has this workflow, uses any named source, or needs to change it now.
assumed_experiences: Profile-supported: I am responsible for product decisions at a software company.
Email-only and conditional: customer feedback reaches my team through calls, tickets, or reviews.
Email-only: full conversations are currently being handled as feedback units rather than individual requests.
Email-only: duplicate requests create enough review work to make automatic merging useful.
Unknown: my current feedback repository, integrations, volume, and willingness to replace or supplement an existing process.
reads.problem_now: Request-level extraction and duplicate merging address a documented product-feedback problem, so the premise is relevant. Whether it is a problem for my team right now, at meaningful volume, is unknown; the profile establishes neither urgency nor our current intake process.
reads.biggest_doubt: I cannot tell whether Canny can ingest the particular sources my team uses or how much connection, permission, and review setup is required before its extracted requests become usable. The unexplained reference to pausing upgrades also makes the Free plan's billing behavior less reassuring than intended.
reads.to_click_it_would_have_to: I would have clicked if this email had told me which source types or connectors the Free plan supports and what the smallest test requires—for example, connecting one source or importing one conversation without changing our existing workflow.
fixes: Rewrite “If customer feedback arrives through calls, tickets, or reviews, Canny Autopilot reads those sources” to specify how those sources are connected or imported and which ones can be tested on the Free plan.
Rewrite “It brings feedback into one place” to say where the extracted requests appear and what I can do with them during review; the current line repeats the general promise.
Cut or clarify “You can set a monthly spend limit to pause upgrades when it is reached” because it introduces unexplained automatic upgrades and billing mechanics before I understand the trial setup.

Rewrite “Create a Free account to see whether request extraction and duplicate merging fit your team’s intake process” as a concrete first test, including the minimum source, permissions, and setup required.
reads.material_revision: Explain the operating path from a source to a reviewable request: how I connect or import feedback, where extracted requests appear, and what the product team can review or approve before anything enters the organized feedback set. Without that, I understand the promise but cannot picture testing it safely within our current intake process.
